London, 27<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Chrysler and the UAW** agreed to revised labor terms that may help the automaker forge an alliance with Fiat S.p.A. and qualify for additional U.S. rescue loans. The union said Chrysler, Fiat and the U.S. Treasury Department agreed to the deal.  Workers must approve the terms by Wednesday. No details were offered. Like an accord with the Canadian Auto Workers announced Friday and ratified today, the UAW concessions don’t include a wage cut, said a source familiar with the talks. The UAW concessions are at least as deep as those settled by the CAW, the source said. Those CAW savings were pegged at about C$240 million ($198 million) annually.   The CAW said its members voted 87% in favour of their new collective agreement with Chrysler, which has about 8,000 unionized workers in Canada. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**General Motors Corp.,** working to beat a June 1 U.S.-ordered bankruptcy deadline, will provide details today on the latest plan to cut costs and keep $15.4 billion in U.S. loans it needs to survive.  The automaker will discuss elimination of the Pontiac brand and reductions in plants and employees as well as initiatives to complete cuts as much as four years sooner than planned, people briefed on the details said. GM will update the news media at 9 a.m. New York time. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**New car production in the UK** fell by 51% in March, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders, compared to the 59pc reported in February. In the year to date, car production is down 56.6pc to 183,010, commercial production down 63pc and total vehicle manufacturing 57.4pc.  The UK government recently announced a scrappage scheme that involves consumers receiving £1,000 from the state and £1,000 from the industry towards scrapping their car of over 10-years-old for a new model. The scheme will be worth £600m in total and was broadly welcomed by the industry. _Source:  The Telegraph_ 

**GM** will have a nine-week summer  shut down at most of its North American plants, which could bankrupt as many as 10% of GMs top 3-00 parts makers. GM spokesman Dan Flores declined to comment on the likelihood of bankruptcies.  But he acknowledged that the lengthy production shutdown will cause cashflow crises among suppliers. _Source: Automotive News_ 

Gauged interest indicates **Magma Metals Ltd** may be oversubscribed in its planned raising of $A16 million ($US M) through issuing 50 M new shares at A32 cents - a placement which Anglo American plc participated in to maintain its 12% stake in the company.  The raising, with Perth stockbroker Hartleys Ltd as lead manager, was being taken up by domestic and international investors to provide fresh capital for the Thunder Bay North platinum-palladium-copper-nickel prospect in Ontario.  Interest in Magma was sharpened by the release this week of a spectacular round of drilling results from the Current Lake-Beaver Lake are

a at Thunder Bay North, where drilling has been on a 3 kilometre strike.  Latest results included hole TBND134 which had 37 metres grading 4.55 grams/tonne combined platinum-palladium, 0.49% copper and 0.26% nickel, including 22m @ 6.52 g/t Pt-Pd, 0.69% Cu and 0.33% Ni; and hole TBND171 with 40.45m @ 7.12 g/t Pt-Pd, 0.84% Cu and 0.41% Ni, including 9m @ 10.68 g/t Pt-Pd, 1.21% Cu and 0.5% Ni.  Magma has now completed 26,500m of drilling at Thunder Bay North.  MD Keith Watkins said the new capital would be sued to complete definition drilling and resource estimates as well as stepout drilling to extend the resource to the south east.  Watkins said the placement will be completed in two tranches, with an initial 15 M shares to raise $A4.8 M by utilising the company’s placement capacity under ASX rules - expected to be completed next week. The remaining share placement is conditional on shareholder approval, to be sought at a meeting late in May. _Source:  Mineweb_
